title: Kasuti (counted-thread embroidery)
summary: Kasuti is the counted-thread embroidery of Karnataka, in southern India. Makers count the threads of the cloth and work tiny straight stitches in single rows, so the pattern looks the same on both faces; traditional border and chessboard motifs repeat in red, green and white on dark cloth.
howToPlay: Pick a thread colour and a stitch pattern from the tray.
Touch a square on the cloth to stitch that pattern there; its mirror partners are stitched too.
Copy the thread chart beside the cloth, then press Check.
rules: The design mirrors left to right and top to bottom, so each stitch you place is also worked on its partner squares.
A square counts only when its stitch pattern and its thread colour both match the chart.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Kasuti has been worked by women in Karnataka for centuries, traditionally on saree borders and blouse yokes. Its counted stitches and fixed motif families, passed from mother to daughter, are still taught in homes and craft schools.
credits: Pattern design: World Heritage Games (original arrangements in the style of the tradition)
